statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Online; bconline.gov.bc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A British Columbia business corporation name must contain a distinct element followed by a legal element such as 'Ltd.', 'Corp.', 'Inc.', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or 'Ltee'. Names may be in English or French; if a name is in another language, it must be transliterated into Latin script for registry indexing. The name must not mislead the public, be identical or confusing to existing corporate or trade names, and numbers, punctuation, and special characters are restricted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If BC Registries refuses a Name Request, the applicant receives a written reason. Within 30 days of refusal, the applicant may submit a reconsideration request with legal arguments and evidence of non-confusing use in the BC or Canadian marketplace. If reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may file a new Name Request after curing the cited defects or apply for judicial review before the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is generally permissible for this AdTech platform if the registered office is a real street address in British Columbia, service of process is accepted, and statutory records are kept and accessible at that address. A mere virtual mailbox without physical presence may be rejected by BC Registries.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated annual probability below 5%) for a low-risk, non-regulated ISIC 7310 programmatic advertising company; no routine physical inspections are conducted by BC Registries, but police and tax authorities may attend for cause.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), SBC 2002, c. 57, ss. 10(1) (incorporation), 12 (notice of articles), 13 (incorporation agreement), 51 (authorized share structure), 173 (first directors), and 221 (minute books).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Citizens' Services, Victoria, British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1) and Notice of Articles (Form 2) filed through BC Corporate Online
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the BC Business Corporations Act; shares may be issued at a nominal price. The directors fix the consideration and allotment in accordance with the Notice of Articles. No escrow account is required; subscription funds may be placed in the Corporation's operating bank account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the Corporation accept subscriptions for 100,000 common shares at CAD 0.01 per share from each subscribing founder and issue such shares for the consideration specified in the subscription agreements. (2) That the registered and records office be established at [Registered Office Address], British Columbia, and that the address be filed with the BC Corporate Registry. (3) That [Director A] be appointed as President, [Director B] as Secretary, and [Director C] as Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting. (4) That the President and Secretary are authorised to open bank accounts and sign all operational documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services – Corporate Registry Name Reservation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) test through the BC Corporate Online portal; verify corporate name distinction and trademark conflicts; submit a name reservation application with the proposed name and applicant declaration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar objects to the name due to conflict with an existing corporate or trademark, file a written reconsideration with the Corporate Registry or select a revised distinctive name and pay the re-reservation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Statutory Organization Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporating legal counsel / notary public (pre-filing) and BC Corporate Registry (ultimate filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Incorporation Application (Form 1), Notice of Articles (Form 2), Incorporation Agreement and consent-to-act forms; have all subscribers/directors execute and witness signatures; digitally notarize signatures if required.
required_dossiers: Form 2 – Notice of Articles (share structure, restrictions, officer/director information)
Directors' consents to act as first directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registrar review queries are resolved by filing a corrected Notice of Articles or a supplementary declaration through Corporate Online; if rejection is issued, amend and refile within 90 days of the initial application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation package via Corporate Online; pay the incorporation filing fee by credit card or BC ePay; upon approval, download the Certificate of Incorporation and stamped Notice of Articles.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and records office address in British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned for technical defects, correct the defects and resubmit; if the certificate is refused on discretionary grounds, file a court application or invoke the restorative provisions of the Business Corporations Act after consulting counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Share Issue and Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation; authorised officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or obtain a consent resolution; approve the share subscription agreements, determine share consideration, adopt the first board resolution; approve the registered office, appoint officers, open bank accounts and issue share certificates.
required_dossiers: Notice of first meeting of directors (if in-person)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer consent is missing, obtain written consent prior to acting; if the bank requires enhanced beneficial ownership disclosure, provide an organizational chart and beneficial ownership register to satisfy regulatory requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online; BC Ministry of Finance (Consumers' Taxation Branch)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with CRA for a nine-digit Business Number; open accounts for corporate income tax, GST/HST, and payroll if employees are hired; register for BC provincial sales tax under the Social Service Tax Act through the combined one-stop business registration process.
required_dossiers: Directors' personal identification and social insurance numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the application, respond through Represent a Client to verify officers; if the Business Number issuance is delayed, request a provisional BN confirmation letter from the CRA Business Window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Occupational Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Business Licence Department (e.g., City of Vancouver Business Licence & Development Services) and WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence based on the corporation's registered office and any physical service location; provide lease agreements and occupancy certificates; if staff are employed, register the employer with WorkSafeBC; obtain fire safety and building occupancy inspections if required by the municipality.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal licensing refuses due to incomplete zone or premise compliance, remedy by correcting zoning or filing an appeal to the municipal board of variance; if WorkSafeBC classification is disputed, request a reconsideration under the Workers Compensation Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — competent national authority for corporate income tax (T2), GST/HST, payroll (RP) and import/export (RM) accounts. Registration and compliance portals: Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html). Provincial indirect tax authority for the British Columbia (CA-BC) seat: BC Ministry of Finance, eTaxBC portal (https://etax.gov.bc.ca) for Provincial Sales Tax (PST) and Employer Health Tax (EHT).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1 — Entity residence: as a corporation incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act (or BC Business Corporations Act), the entity is a Canadian resident under ITA s. 250(4)(a) and a per se taxable corporation. STEP 2 — Business Number (federal TIN): incorporate first with Corporations Canada or the BC Registry; upon incorporation the 9-digit Business Number (BN) is issued, and the entity must activate program accounts through CRA BRO, or by filing Form RC1 or, for non-resident applicants, Form RC1A (Request for a Non-Resident Account), mailbox or online. STEP 3 — GST/HST account: open the RT program account under ETA s. 240 if taxable supplies in Canada exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold; voluntary registration is permitted (binding 12 months) to claim input tax credits. STEP 4 — Payroll and import/export accounts: open RP payroll account if employees are in Canada, and RM customs account for the import or export of goods; the platform's digital export services typically require no RM account. STEP 5 — Mandatory CRA e-services: enroll in My Business Account and submit the T2 corporate return electronically (mandatory for corporations with gross revenue over CAD 1,000,000) and GST/HST returns electronically (mandatory for registrants whose annual worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 1,500,000). STEP 6 — BC provincial registrations: register for PST with eTaxBC as a vendor before making taxable retail sales of goods, software or prescribed services in BC (no de minimis sales threshold); register for EHT if BC remuneration exceeds CAD 500,000. STEP 7 — Records: maintain books and records under ITA s. 230(1) and ETA s. 286(1), including all export-side counterparty evidence for zero-rated entitlements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no 'check-the-box' entity classification election (unlike U.S. Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3); the Business Corporation is a per se taxable corporation resident in Canada. Available elections material to this AdTech platform: (i) ETA s. 156 election between closely related corporations to treat intercorporate supplies as made for nil consideration; (ii) ETA s. 240 voluntary GST/HST registration election for a non-resident or small supplier, binding for at least 12 months and required to recover ITCs; (iii) GST/HST Quick Method of Accounting for eligible small registered suppliers; (iv) ITA s. 249.1 fiscal-period election to shorten/lengthen a taxation year (Canadian resident corporations other than CCPCs may elect a non-calendar fiscal period); (v) ITA s. 125(7) associated-corporations allocation to apportion the small business deduction among associated Canadian-controlled private corporations; (vi) hybrid mismatch rules, ITA ss. 18.2–18.3, are mandatory computerational provisions (BEPS Action 2), with no affirmative election. Cross-border, a foreign seller may elect into the simplified GST/HST registration for non-residents (ETA s. 241.1); the Canadian resident entity does not file such election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST Value-Added Tax (federal); British Columbia applies the 5% GST plus a separate 7% Provincial Sales Tax (PST, retail/usage tax, not creditable), plus BC Employer Health Tax (EHT) on payroll over CAD 500,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 (small-supplier threshold) measured on worldwide taxable supplies, excluding zero-rated exports, in the current calendar quarter and the preceding four calendar quarters; registration is mandatory within 30 days of crossing the limit, otherwise voluntary. BC PST: every 'vendor' making retail sales of taxable goods, software, and specified services into British Columbia must register in eTaxBC — there is no de minimis sales threshold equivalent to the GST small-supplier rule. BC EHT: registration required when total BC remuneration exceeds CAD 500,000 in a calendar year.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently impose real-time fiscal clearance, government-side digital stamping, or mandatory CRA API validation ('CFDI-style') on B2B invoices. Standard compliance: each GST/HST invoice must contain the supplier's legal or trading name, 9-digit BN/RM number, invoice date, description of the supply, total consideration and either the GST/HST amount, or a statement that GST/PST is included (ETA s. 223; Input Tax Credit Information Regulations SOR/2007-224). GST/HST returns and T2 returns must be e-filed (NETFILE/XML) once the applicable revenue thresholds are reached. CRA is gradually adopting the Peppol/PAN-Canadian e-invoicing framework announced in 2024, but participation remains voluntary as of the current mandate window. For an AdTech platform, each settlement payment to a Canadian media source must also be supported by a complete tax-payment trail, and incoming international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more transit the reporting obligations of the Canadian payment service provider under the PCMLTFA/FINTRAC reporting regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for (A) goods: a supply of tangible personal property is zero-rated under ETA Sch. VI, Part V where the supplier exports it by or on behalf of the supplier within 60 days, evidenced by a customs export declaration; and (B) services and intangible personal property: a supply of a service or IP made to a non-resident person is zero-rated unless the supply is in respect of Canadian-situated real or tangible property, is a 'personal service' performed in Canada, or is made to a non-resident who is a GST/HST registrant for a Canadian business. For the programmatic DSP/SSP platform, the following qualify as zero-rated exports: (i) software access, data-reporting, and SSP bidding services supplied to non-resident advertisers, publishers, and agency counterparties not using the services in their Canadian commercial activities; (ii) ad inventory brokering and ad-serving fees charged to foreign media owners where the underlying inventory is sold outside Canada. Services supplied to Canadian-domiciled advertisers, or for campaigns targeting Canadian-resident consumers where the recipient is Canadian, bear 5% GST. The exporter must maintain contemporaneous documentation that the recipient is non-resident and the supply is not consumed in Canada. Registration for GST/HST permits the platform to claim input tax credits and obtain periodic refunds where zero-rated exports exceed Canadian taxable supplies; ITCs must be claimed within four years of the due date of the reporting period in which the expense was incurred (ETA s. 225(2); s. 228(6)).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Signed export service agreement / order confirmation evidencing the non-resident counterparty, scope (SSP/DSP software access, bidding and reporting services) and fee schedule.
GST/HST zero-rated invoice satisfying ETA s. 223 and SOR/2007-224, noting 'zero-rated export — Schedule VI, Part V'.
Non-residency attestation from the counterparty (W-8BEN-E, certificate of residence, or foreign incorporation extract) confirming no Canadian permanent establishment involvement.
Inward remittance evidence: SWIFT MT103 / ACH credit adviser and bank statement showing FX repatriation to the Canadian operating account within 180 days.
Platform delivery and settlement logs (impression counts, DSP/SSP auction records, publisher payout reports) proving actual performance of the exported service.

Where tangible promotional goods accompany the service: Canada Customs B13A Export Declaration, commercial invoice, bill of lading/airway bill and inward/outward manifest retained for CRA verification.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA audits export zero-rating on a risk-weighted basis; the registrant bears the burden of proving the export character and non-residency of the recipient. Where documentation is absent or contemporaneity fails, the CRA may deny zero-rating, reassess net tax on the full consideration as if GST had been charged, and impose: (i) arrears interest at the prescribed corporate daily compound rate (currently 8% base for corporate arrears, set quarterly) from the date the GST/HST was otherwise due; (ii) under ETA s. 280, a penalty of 5% of any net tax that the registrant failed to remit, or 25% where the misstatement was made knowingly or under circumstances amounting to gross negligence in respect of an ITC or rebate; (iii) gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the tax understated on the T2 under ITA s. 163(2), with criminal prosecution under ITA s. 239(1) for deliberate evasion. The ordinary reassessment window is four years (ETA s. 298(2); ITA s. 152(4)), but the Crown may reassess at any time on misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, or willful default. Export declarations for goods made with false statements trigger penalties under Customs Act s. 127 (up to CAD 10,000 and/or 50% of the value of the goods). Provincially, failure to register for BC PST exposes the vendor to the unregistered-vendor assessment equal to 7% PST on taxable sales, plus a 10% late-payment penalty and BC interest on arrears; all amounts remain retroactively assessable for up to four years in the absence of misrepresentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (the federal central bank and monetary authority), together with the Department of Finance Canada which administers the Exchange Fund Account; Canada maintains no dedicated foreign exchange control administration and no exchange-control licensing regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII jurisdiction with full convertibility of the Canadian dollar for both current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no exchange controls, no surrender requirements, no approval gates for dividend or management-fee remittances, and no distinction between resident and non-resident remittance eligibility. Profit repatriation from a British Columbia business corporation is lawful and unrestricted under the federal Currency Act, the Bank of Canada Act, and the BC Business Corporations Act. The only material statutory screen is the Investment Canada Act: a foreign non-Canadian acquiring control of an existing Canadian business above the prescribed monetary thresholds may require a net-benefit review filing, but an organic incorporation of a new BC corporation by non-residents is not a reviewable acquisition. ISIC 7310 programmatic advertising is not classified as a cultural business, so the lower cultural-business review thresholds do not apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender rule, no statutory conversion timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export or service receipts, including USD revenues earned by an AdTech DSP/SSP platform, may be retained indefinitely in foreign-currency bank accounts inside or outside Canada. The only compliance obligations are: (i) FINTRAC cross-border electronic funds transfer reports for wire transfers of CAD 10,000 or more in a single transaction or within 24 hours, filed by the bank; and (ii) Canada Revenue Agency Form T1135 disclosure on specified foreign property where the aggregate cost of foreign assets, including offshore cash accounts and receivables, exceeds CAD 100,000. Dividend and interest outflows to non-resident shareholders require no central bank approval; only standard withholding taxes under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act apply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium. Canada has no statutory EMI licence or passporting regime comparable to the EU. Cross-border fintech payment providers, including Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, and dLocal, generally operate either as FINTRAC-registered Money Service Businesses (MSBs) for foreign-exchange dealing and money transfers or as Payment Service Providers (PSPs) subject to the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) administered by the Bank of Canada, with mandatory registration and compliance obligations under the deferred-application phase. These platforms offer materially lower-cost multi-currency clearing and are legally viable for ancillary disbursements to overseas publishers and data suppliers. However, a Tier 1 Schedule I Canadian bank remains the only institution capable of providing a segregated capital/escrow account, a domestic CAD clearing framework, OSFI-protected deposit insurance, and a full transactional banking relationship. Recommendation: maintain core liquidity at a Tier 1 bank and use an MSB/RPPA fintech only as a secondary settlement rail for low-value, high-volume programmatic payouts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is functionally required for non-resident directors of a newly incorporated, foreign-controlled BC corporation. While FINTRAC's Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act regulations permit identity verification through reliable electronic sources, all Canadian Schedule I banks conduct risk-based enhanced due diligence for such accounts and routinely mandate at least one of the following: (a) an in-person interview at an RBC/TD/BMO/Scotiabank/CIBC branch, typically in Vancouver, BC; (b) a live video-verified meeting with a designated relationship manager with notarized identification; or (c) a hybrid process requiring physical delivery of certified corporate registry documents, a certified board resolution appointing signatories, and an original or apostilled notarized passport copy for each director and the ultimate beneficial owner. Remote-only digital onboarding is normally unavailable to a newly incorporated foreign-owned corporation with no established Canadian trading history. The account class, expected wire velocity, and cross-border payment profile will trigger additional management-level credit and compliance review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign UBO with a multi-jurisdiction holding chain and opaque intermediate entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organizational chart from the operating entity to each ultimate individual; certified registry extracts for every intermediate holding company; statutory declaration of source of funds and source of wealth; audited financial statements or a consolidated group report; notarized passport copies of directors and UBOs; and a professional bank reference letter from the UBO's primary non-Canadian bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity digital advertising flows creating unexplained transaction patterns (DSP/SSP programmatic settlements)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts with major ad exchanges and supply-side platforms (Google Ad Manager, DV360, The Trade Desk, PubMatic); monthly platform settlement and auction reconciliation reports; documented treasury policy establishing the commercial purpose for each wire class; segregation of client media funds from operating cash; and an AML/ATF compliance program summary if the entity holds payment accounts for counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a tight-fund jurisdiction with limited supporting ownership trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorizing the capital call and share subscription; the foreign bank's credit statement of the remitting account; SWIFT MT103 copy showing remitter, beneficiary, and stated purpose; certificate of incorporation of the foreign parent; and a source-of-wealth statement signed by the funder, with corroborating financial statements if the amount exceeds CAD 1,000,000.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdictional mismatch where beneficial ownership is traced to OFAC/EU/UK sanctions-listed or high-risk territories
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Declaration that the UBO and directors have no sanctions or PEP nexus; negative sanctions-screen snapshots from a commercial screening tool for all principals; proof of physical substance in Canada (lease agreement, payroll register, BC registrations, office photographs); and a narrative memo explaining the commercial rationale for the BC establishment and the foreign ownership structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: inbound share-capital is delivered by SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent's or shareholder's bank to the BC corporation's Schedule I Canadian bank account, referencing the board resolution number, the share subscription agreement, and a clear remittance narrative, e.g. 'Equity Capital Contribution' or 'Share Capital Injection – ISIC 7310 AdTech Treasury'. Canada does not mandate a national purpose-code registry; banks apply their own transactional classification but require the narrative to intelligibly match the flow. CAD-denominated injections settle over Payments Canada Lynx (real-time gross settlement) or the ACSS; USD injections settle via the bank's US correspondent clearing network (typically through New York CHIPS or Fedwire). The receiving bank will file a FINTRAC cross-border EFT report for any wire of CAD 10,000 or more. The client treasury file must hold: the certified board resolution, the updated share register, evidence of the source account, and, where applicable, any Investment Canada Act filing or exemption note. No Canadian central bank authorization or pre-notification is required for the capital injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 via Fedwire or CHIPS for high-value USD payouts to media supply partners, data providers, and inventory licences; (2) Automated Clearing House (ACH/NACHA) for recurring low-value USD settlements to US ad exchanges and publishers; (3) Payments Canada Lynx and ACSS electronic funds transfer for domestic CAD disbursements to Canadian suppliers and operating vendors; (4) Commercial Letter of Credit issued through SWIFT MT700 for larger media procurement or data-supply contracts requiring documentary guarantees, with conforming documents presented under UCP600; and (5) a dedicated USD non-resident or Canadian USD clearing account to minimize CAD/USD conversion friction. The treasury architecture must separate client/principal funds from the corporation's own operating funds where the platform holds cash for counterparties, and must maintain audit-ready reconciliation between DSP cash-flow reports, SSP settlement statements, and bank debit/credit advices.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD outright forwards traded with a Schedule I Canadian bank under standard Master FX Terms, tenors up to 12–24 months
CAD/USD FX swaps and rollovers for rolling settlement of recurring USD-denominated media purchases
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic-currency payouts to publishers or vendors in restricted-deliverability jurisdictions encountered by the programmatic supply network
Vanilla CAD/USD FX options (call and put) to hedge budgeted ad-inventory purchases against adverse CAD/USD moves

Cross-currency swaps (CAD-USD) to match long-term USD receivables from ad exchanges against CAD operating costs, executed under an ISDA Master Agreement with the corporate treasury as a commercial end-user

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Registrar of Companies (BC Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after each anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 70 if filed after the due date; failure to file for two consecutive years may trigger administrative strike-off or dissolution by the registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (if federally incorporated)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of federal incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing charges under the CBCA; prolonged non-compliance beyond six months may lead to administrative dissolution of the corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the end of the corporation's taxation year (June 30 for a calendar-year corporate)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty under subsection 162(1) of the Income Tax Act: 5% of any unpaid balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeated non-filing may result in prosecution or summary conviction.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is mandatory for public companies and other prescribed reporting issuers. A private BC corporation may dispense with an auditor through a unanimous shareholder resolution under the BC Business Corporations Act. CRA may require an audit for tax assurance purposes irrespective of corporate requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Canada for public issuers; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for eligible private corporations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: British Columbia does not require a separate annual UBO return to the corporate registry. However, the internal Transparency Register (Individuals with Significant Control) must be reviewed and updated at least annually to coincide with the annual report cycle, and any triggering events must be recorded within seven days as per the BC Business Corporations Act.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - USD 500 per annum depending on BC registered office / filing agent provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,600 - USD 5,600 if a voluntary or required compilation, review, or audit is engaged for a private BC corporate
